articles.summary: United front is short-lived as Zia Yusuf and Chris Philp bicker in front of residents and cameras Archbishop of Canterbury Sarah Mullally has said “people are seeking meaning, connection and hope in a turbulent world” as new statistics reveal Church of England attendances have grown for the fifth year in a row. Whether at morning prayer, a Sunday service, Evensong, a youth hub, a parent and toddler group - or any of the countless ways that the Church of England serves our communities in every parish - it is clear that people are seeking meaning, connection and hope in a turbulent world. articles.title: Nigel Farage’s security paid for by Reform UK despite claim over £5m gift
articles.summary: Exclusive: Sources reveal party is covering costs – raising new questions about leader’s explanation for billionaire’s gift Nigel Farage’s personal security has been paid for out of Reform UK’s central funds despite his claim that these expenses would be covered by an undisclosed gift of £5m from a billionaire donor, sources have told the Guardian. The Reform leader has had the central party pay for a team and two cars ever since a reduction in the security provided by the taxpayer after a review in 2025. Continue reading...

articles.title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
articles.summary: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium on Thursday, ending two years of gang control. Salvadoran troops have now taken over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush in which four of its troops went missing.

articles.title: 'Devastated wasteland': Haitian security forces regain control of stadium from gangs
articles.summary: Haitian security forces said they have regained control of the country's main stadium, wresting it back from the gangs that have been using it for the past two years. They were assisted by the Task Force, a private security group serving the government. The stadium is now under the guard of Salvadoran soldiers. FRANCE 24's senior reporter Catherine Norris Trent, who has covered Haiti extensively, said re-taking the stadium would be a significant step in an area of the city that had been a "devastated wasteland".

articles.title: Indonesia's wiretapping scandal opens a political fault line
articles.summary: Senior police officers are accused of illegally monitoring President Prabowo Subianto, exposing rival networks within Indonesia's security establishment and renewing concerns about political misuse of surveillance.
